comments.content: Making checkpoint creation fire-and-forget introduces two risks: 1) `this.checkpointTracker.commit().then(...)` has no `.catch`, so a rejected git operation will cause an unhandled promise rejection and the user will still see a 'checkpoint_created' message with no hash. 2) The message index is looked up with `findLastIndex` only when the commit resolves. If another checkpoint is created before the first commit finishes, the later 'checkpoint_created' message will be the last one found and will be updated with the earlier commit hash. Capture the message index immediately after `await this.say('checkpoint_created')` and add error handling for the background commit.
